newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court finds judicial security requirement discriminatory.
newsitem.headline: Court finds judicial security requirement discriminatory.

text.p: The European Court of Justice told a Swedish court on Thursday that it may not require a national from another member state to lodge a security if none is required from a Swedish national.

When a British company sought relief in a Swedish court for payment on goods delivered against Swedish companies, the defendants asked the court to require the company to place in escrow funds necessary to cover judicial costs.
Although a 1980 Swedish law requires such security, the Swedish District Court found that the 1988 Lugano Convention superceded the earlier law and that none was needed.
The Swedish defendants appealed to the Supreme Court, which asked the European court to review Community law.

The court said that national rules on civil procedure fell within the scope of non-discrimination policies under article 6 of the EC Treaty, and that a provision such as the 1980 Swedish law was manifestly discriminatory.
The court said Sweden could not require a security to cover judicial costs from citizens of other member states unless it also required one for Swedish nationals.
(Court translation into English. Original language of the case: Swedish)
"Equal treatment - Discrimination on the grounds of nationality - Security for the costs of judicial proceedings"
Reference from the Hogsta Domstolen, Stockholm, for a preliminary ruling in the proceedings pending before that court between
on the interpretation of article 6 of the EC Treaty

The first paragraph of article 6 of the EC Treaty precludes a member state from requiring a legal person established in another member state which has brought, before one of its courts, an action against one of its nationals or a company established in the member state in question to lodge security for the costs of proceedings, where no such requirement can be imposed on legal persons from that state, in a situation in which the action is connected with the exercise of fundamental freedoms guaranteed by Community law.
